'''Ran Nathan''' ({{Langx|he|רן נתן}}; born 1962) is an Israeli biologist, [[Ornithology|ornithologist]], and academic.

He is an [[ecology|ecologist]] who holds the Adelina and Massimo Della Pergola Chair of life Sciences at the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]]<ref>[https://www.bio.huji.ac.il/staff_in.asp?staff_id=57 Ran Nathan, Dept. of Ecology, Evolution & Behavior]</ref><ref name=RanCV>[http://www.huji.ac.il/dataj/controller/ihoker/MOP-STAFF_LINK?sno=5373688&Save_t The Division for Advancement and External Relations, HUJI]</ref> in the Department of Ecology, Evolution and Behavior<ref>[http://eeb.huji.ac.il/ The Department of Ecology, Evolution and Behavior, HUJI]</ref> where he leads the Movement Ecology Lab.<ref name=RanMovEcol>[https://huji.move-ecol.com/users/ran-nathan Movement Ecology Lab website]</ref> Additionally, Nathan is the director of the Minerva Center for Movement Ecology<ref name=MinervaCenter/> and the co-founding co-Editor-in-Chief of the free-access journal ''Movement Ecology'' (BioMed Central).<ref name=MovJournal>[https://movementecologyjournal.biomedcentral.com/about/editorial-board Movement Ecology Journal Editorial Board]</ref>

His work focuses on various aspects of movement ecology, including dispersal (and long-distance dispersal in particular), migration, foraging, navigation, flight aerodynamics, animal behavior, social interactions, invasive species, disease spread by avian species, gene flow, plant-animal interactions and plant recruitment.<ref name=RanCV/><ref name=RanMovEcol/>

==Research interests==
===Long-distance dispersal===

Nathan's earlier work (since 1999) focused on [[seed dispersal]], and long-distance dispersal (LDD) in particular. In a series of studies, he and his colleagues demonstrated the strength of the mechanistic approach in understanding seed dispersal<ref name=SeedDispersalNature>[https://www.nature.com/nature/journal/v418/n6896/abs/nature00844.html Mechanisms of long-distance dispersal of seeds by wind, Nature, 2002]</ref> and plant dynamics,<ref name=SpatialTREE>{{cite journal| doi=10.1016/S0169-5347(00)01874-7 | pmid=10856948 | volume=15 | issue=7 | title=Spatial patterns of seed dispersal, their determinants and consequences for recruitment | year=2000 | journal=Trends in Ecology & Evolution | pages=278–285 | last1 = Nathan | first1 = Ran | last2 = Muller-Landau | first2 = Helene C.}}</ref> as well as the importance of rare long-distance dispersal events in plants (Nathan 2006 ''Science''), their underlying mechanisms<ref name=MechanismsTREE>{{cite journal| doi=10.1016/j.tree.2008.08.003 |pmid = 18823680| volume=23 | issue=11 | title=Mechanisms of long-distance seed dispersal | year=2008 | journal=Trends in Ecology & Evolution | pages=638–647 | last1 = Nathan | first1 = Ran | last2 = Schurr | first2 = Frank M. | last3 = Spiegel | first3 = Orr | last4 = Steinitz | first4 = Ofer | last5 = Trakhtenbrot | first5 = Ana | last6 = Tsoar | first6 = Asaf| bibcode=2008TEcoE..23..638N }}</ref> and their role in determining spread rates of plants in future environments.<ref name="ReferenceA">{{cite journal|doi=10.1111/j.1461-0248.2010.01573.x | pmid=21251175 | volume=14 | issue=3 | title=Spread of North American wind-dispersed trees in future environments | year=2011 | journal=Ecology Letters | pages=211–219 | last1 = Nathan | first1 = Ran| bibcode=2011EcolL..14..211N | citeseerx=10.1.1.459.2341 }}</ref>

===Movement ecology===
In an interview for Science Watch (October 2010),<ref>[http://archive.sciencewatch.com/inter/aut/2010/10-oct/10octNath/ Ran Nathan on the Growing Importance of Movement Ecology, Science Watch]</ref> Nathan revealed that the idea to establish movement ecology as a new field of research was born in 2002, when he was a first-year faculty member supervising one student on seed dispersal and another on bird migration, facing the question “what name should I call my research group”? This has led him to wonder why different movement phenomena are studied in isolation from each other, and why there is still no general unifying theory of organismal movement. He then decided to call his research group "movement ecology", and later on noticed this term has already been used in the literature, but very occasionally at the time and never in the context of a unifying research paradigm.

In 2006, Nathan initiated and led an international group at the [[Israel Institute for Advanced Studies]] in Jerusalem<ref>[http://www.as.huji.ac.il/ Israeli Institute for Advanced Studies in Jerusalem]</ref> which has set the foundation for development of the field of movement ecology as a new integration of movement research. In 2008, he edited a Special Feature on Movement Ecology<ref>[http://www.pnas.org/content/105/49.toc#MovementEcologySpecialFeature Movement Ecology Special Feature, PNAS, 2008]</ref> for the Proceedings of the National Academy of USA.<ref name=PNAS>[http://www.pnas.org/ Proceedings of the National Academy of USA]</ref> This collection included a perspective paper introducing the basic concepts and a framework for integrating movement research.<ref name=ParadigmPNAS>[http://www.pnas.org/content/105/49/19052.full A movement ecology paradigm for unifying organismal movement research, PNAS, 2008]</ref><ref>[http://www.pnas.org/content/105/49/19050.full An emerging movement ecology paradigm, PNAS, 2008]</ref> In 2012, Nathan established the Minerva Center for Movement Ecology<ref name=MinervaCenter/> supported by the [[Minerva Foundation]]<ref name=MinervaFoundation>[https://www.minerva.mpg.de/ Minerva Foundation]</ref> and the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]] as a German-Israeli interdisciplinary research center for studying movement ecology. Together with Prof. Sivan Toledo (Computer Sciences, [[Tel Aviv University]]),<ref name=SivanToledo>[http://www.tau.ac.il/~stoledo/ Sivan Toledo, TAU]</ref> he developed a revolutionary wildlife tracking system called ATLAS (Advanced Tracking and Localization of Animals in real-life Systems), a portable, affordable tracking system capable of automatically and simultaneously tracking a large number of small animals (20 grams and less) in high accuracy and high sampling frequency.<ref name=ATLAS>[http://move-ecol-minerva.huji.ac.il/page/3 The ATLAS project]</ref><ref>[https://www.dw.com/en/flying-with-the-birds/a-19004408 Flying with the birds, Deutsche Welle]</ref> In 2013, Nathan co-founded a new open-access journal, ''Movement Ecology'' (BioMed Central),<ref>[https://movementecologyjournal.biomedcentral.com/ Movement Ecology Journal website]</ref> which has become a major forum for publishing studies on the movement of animals and plants.

==Education, appointments, professional activity and honors==
===Education===

*[[Bachelor of Science]] in Biology (with distinction), [[The Hebrew University of Jerusalem]], Israel, 1989–1992.
*[[Ph.D.]] in Ecology (Supervisors: Profs. U. N. Safriel and I. Noy-Meir), The Hebrew University of Jerusalem, Israel, Department of Evolution, Systematics and Ecology (now Department of Ecology, Evolution and Behavior, 1994–2000
*Post-Doctoral Fellow and Research Associate (Supervisor: Prof. S. A. Levin), [[Princeton University]], Department of Ecology and Evolutionary Biology, 1999–2001

===Appointments===

*Lecturer, [[Ben Gurion University of the Negev]], Israel, 2001–2003<ref name=RanCV/><ref name=AsianCamp>[http://cms.education.gov.il/NR/rdonlyres/8EE66D71-8FCB-4827-A063-619B0FEB3EF0/154804/asiancamp2012_mail.pdf Asian Science Camp program, 2012 ]</ref>
*Senior Lecturer, [[Ben Gurion University of the Negev]], Israel, 2003<ref name=RanCV/><ref name=AsianCamp/>
*Senior Lecturer, [[The Hebrew University of Jerusalem]], Israel, 2003–2005<ref name=RanCV/><ref name=AsianCamp/>
*Associate Professor, [[The Hebrew University of Jerusalem]], Israel, 2005–2009<ref name=RanCV/><ref name=AsianCamp/>
*Full Professor, [[The Hebrew University of Jerusalem]], Israel, 2009–present<ref name=RanCV/><ref name=AsianCamp/>

===Selected professional activities===
*Initiator & group leader, Movement Ecology Group (International Research Group at the [[Israel Institute for Advanced Studies]], Jerusalem, Israel), 2006–2007
*Elected Chair, Department of Evolution, Systematics and Ecology (now Department of Ecology, Evolution. and Behavior), The Hebrew University of Jerusalem, Israel, 2007–2009
*Elected Chairman, [[Alexander Silberman Institute of Life Sciences]], The Hebrew University of Jerusalem, Israel, 2009–2011
*Director, Minerva Center for Movement Ecology, Israel, 2012–Present<ref name=MinervaCenter/>
*Visiting Professor, [[Murdoch University]], Australia, 2013
*Vice Dean for Appointments, Faculty of Science, The Hebrew University of Jerusalem, Israel, 2013–2016
*Co-founding co-Editor-in-Chief of Movement Ecology (BMC & Springer, Open-Access)<ref name=MovJournal/>
*Vice Chair, Gordon Research Conference on Animal Movement Ecology, US, March 2017
*Recipient of various research grants: overall raised >11.5 million USD in 42 research grants, 1999–2016
*Invited plenary/keynote speaker in 30 international conferences, >100 invited seminars/lecture, as of Nov. 2016
*Published 112 peer-reviewed publications, including 93 journal articles, 11 book chapters and 8 proceeding papers, as of Nov. 2016
